title: Suffering and God's Purpose
definition: Suffering and God's purpose teach that pain, hardship, loss, and adversity are not meaningless in God's sovereign hands, even when believers cannot fully understand His reasons.
summary: Suffering is never outside God's knowledge, care, or sovereign purpose.
christFocus: Jesus suffered more deeply than any other person and transformed suffering into the means of redemption, demonstrating that God can bring good even from great pain.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Scripture does not teach that all suffering is directly caused by personal sin, nor does it suggest that every hardship can be easily explained. However, it consistently reveals that God remains sovereign over every circumstance. He may use suffering to refine faith, deepen dependence, produce compassion, strengthen character, draw people closer to Himself, or prepare them to minister to others. While believers may not understand every purpose now, they can trust God's wisdom and goodness.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People naturally ask "Why?" during suffering. While Scripture does not answer every question, it assures believers that suffering is never outside God's knowledge, care, or control.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring your questions honestly before God while resisting bitterness and despair. Focus on God's character when His purposes are unclear. Look for opportunities to comfort others with the comfort you have received from Him.
